natalie m: Hi team  was reviewing my prenatal billing and got a denial for "anatomic pathology" for a first-trimester cell-free DNA screen. Hospital billed lab component under a hospital tax ID and carrier says it's out-of-network. I used our in-network OB practice. What do I do?

riley (people-ops): Sorry you're dealing with that, Natalie. Which plan are you on and did you use the network obstetric group? Don't post PHI here.

natalie m: Plus plan, yes I went to Willow OB (in-network). The hospital did the blood draw and billed from their lab subsidiary. Claim # MAT-2026-078. I uploaded the EOB and invoice to the portal.

people-ops-bot: Upload portal: https://benefits.redwood-inc/claims-upload. Carrier lab support line: 1-800-555-CLIN. Reminder: do not post PHI in channel.

tara (benefits): Hi Natalie  thanks for flagging. This is a common split-billing issue: the ordering provider (OB) is in-network but the performing lab or hospital lab may bill from a different tax ID that isn't in-network. For prenatal genetic testing (cfDNA) carriers often require the performing lab to be listed as in-network or processed under the OB group's contract. We'll verify with carrier and the hospital billing office.

natalie m: Is this an appeals thing or can carrier reprocess if I show that Willow OB ordered it?

riley (people-ops): Good question. Tara?

tara (benefits): Typically we: 1) request reprocessing with provider attribution (showing Willow OB as ordering/authorized provider), 2) confirm whether prior auth was required for cfDNA on Plus (often depends on indication), and 3) if carrier still denies, file an appeal. Please DM the last 4 of your member ID and confirm whether a prior auth/CPT authorization was obtained before the draw.

natalie m: DM'd last 4 (6789). No prior auth to my knowledge; OB said it was standard screening. I uploaded the hospital invoice, the OB order, and the EOB.

benefits-intake: Intake ticket created: BP-MAT-2026-310. We've started carrier outreach to request re-adjudication under the ordering provider's contract and to check prior auth rules for CPT 812XX.

people-ops-bot: Carrier note: Sometimes hospitals bill the specimen processing as pathology (separate CPT) which can trigger separate network checks. Have claim # and hospital billing NPI ready when speaking to carrier.

riley (people-ops): Tara, can benefits confirm whether Plus treats routine cfDNA as screening vs diagnostic for auth rules? If retroactive auth is needed, can we request it?

tara (benefits): On Plus, cfDNA for routine screening typically doesn't require prior auth when done per guidelines, but if billed as diagnostic/medical necessity it may. We can request retroactive prior auth/clinical review. We'll also contact the hospital billing team to request re-billing under the OB group's tax ID if applicable.

natalie m: If carrier insists it's OON, what's the reimbursement path? I'm trying to avoid surprise OOP before baby stuff.

tara (benefits): First we pursue reprocessing/appeal. If that fails AND the hospital truly billed from an OON entity, you can submit for out-of-network reimbursement via the portal. Keep originals and any provider letters. Typical timeline: carrier verification 3 business days, reprocessing/appeal 7-14 business days. We'll update ticket BP-MAT-2026-310 in this thread.

natalie m: Thanks. Can benefits also request an itemized bill showing the lab NPI and tax ID? I can forward that to the OB clinic.

benefits-intake: Yes  we've requested an itemized bill from the hospital billing office and asked the carrier to map the billed CPT to the ordering provider. We'll post updates here.

riley (people-ops): Appreciate the fast follow-up. Natalie  we'll keep monitoring and escalate to our carrier rep if no response in 3 business days.

natalie m: Thank you all  much appreciated. :heart:
